title: Solvent-bridged electrolytes for high-energy Li-ion batteries under extreme conditions
abstract: Published online: 27 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41557-026-02221-7 Conventional LiF-forming electrolytes rely on anion-rich Li+ solvation, which inevitably lowers the electrolyte <mark>ionic conductivity</mark> and compromises both fast-charging capabilities and low-temperature performance. Now it has been shown that solvent-bridged electrolytes effectively broaden the liquid range of LiPF6–ether electrolytes, thereby overcoming the intrinsic trade-off between the LiF-rich solid–electrolyte <mark>interphase</mark> and high <mark>ionic conductivity</mark>.

title: Electrochemical upcycling of spent ITO via charge-induced deconstruction
abstract: Published online: 28 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75921-w An electrochemical upcycling strategy for spent indium-tin oxide (ITO) via charge-induced deconstruction. Spent ITO acts directly as the anode, where charge excitation creates oxygen vacancies to release indium and tin ions, deposited as a high-purity In-Sn alloy.

abstract: Doping pseudocapacitive transition metal oxides with metal cations has been demonstrated to enhance the electrochemical performance of the resulting electrode materials, particularly in terms of capacitance, <mark>rate capability</mark>, and cycling stability. title: Room Temperature One-Pot Synthesis of M3B24H23 (M = Na and Li) and Their Investigation as Solid-State Electrolytes
authors: Thi Phuong Thao Nguyen, Wanli Gao, Peter Ó Conghaile, Terry D. Humphries, Craig E. Buckley and Mark Paskevicius
abstract: Conjuncto-type hydridoborates are promising solid electrolytes for battery applications. In this work, the first electrochemical synthesis of M3B24H23 (M = Na and Li), directly from M2B12H12 is reported. A simple, efficient and reliable one-pot synthetic process based on the one-electron oxidation of B12H122− in acetonitrile is proposed. M3B24H23 is produced with the oxidation of B12H122− to the dimeric anion B24H233− at the working electrode (anodic reaction) and reduction of liberated metal ions and protons at the counter electrode (cathodic reaction).
